input.summary: Descriptive pilot using the emulated-netem-v1 runner to observe TCP flow completion time under two delay conditions (0 ms vs. 20 ms added one-way delay) at a fixed emulated bottleneck. No inferential decision rule is included; the server will add descriptive statistics per policy.
clarification_questions: What bottleneck bandwidth and queue size (e.g., 10 Mbit/s, 100-packet BDP buffer) should be held fixed across both conditions, and should the 20 ms delay be applied one-way or round-trip?
What TCP transfer size or duration should be used per flow (e.g., a fixed 10 MB file transfer), and how many parallel flows, if any, should run per replication?
What is your available wall-clock budget and cost ceiling for this pilot, so resource limits can be set appropriately?

proposal.problem: It is unknown whether adding 20 ms of emulated network delay measurably changes TCP flow completion time under otherwise fixed bottleneck conditions in a controlled netem environment.
proposal.question: What are the observed TCP flow completion times under 0 ms versus 20 ms of added emulated delay at a fixed bottleneck, and how do the distributions of those times differ descriptively?
proposal.hypothesis: Under fixed emulated bottleneck conditions, adding 20 ms delay changes TCP flow completion time.
proposal.conditions: Two conditions: (A) 0 ms added delay, fixed bottleneck bandwidth and queue; (B) 20 ms added delay, same fixed bottleneck bandwidth and queue. All other netem parameters held constant.
proposal.related_work: The claim originates from a synthetic networking paper (sha256: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa, retrieved-unreviewed). No full text or prior measurements are available for comparison.
proposal.alternatives: Observed differences in flow completion time could reflect TCP slow-start dynamics, retransmission behaviour, or netem scheduling artefacts rather than the delay manipulation alone; these cannot be separated in this descriptive pilot.
proposal.design: Repeated-measures emulated pilot: each replication runs one TCP transfer under condition A and one under condition B using the netem-v1 runner, with conditions interleaved to reduce ordering effects. Results are reported descriptively.
proposal.metrics: Primary metric: TCP flow completion time (seconds) per transfer. Secondary metric: total bytes transferred per flow (bytes), to verify transfer completeness.
proposal.controls: Bottleneck bandwidth, queue size, loss rate (0%), and transfer size are held fixed. The same netem runner version and host configuration are used for both conditions.
proposal.inputs: No external data files required; transfers are generated internally by the netem runner. Source paper sha256: aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa; packet sha256: a1b401caab0920ee2f11377b7285ff0ef7269c187cfa7f3df1c1cb576ba8c0da.
proposal.limitations: Bottleneck bandwidth, queue size, transfer size, and directionality (one-way vs. round-trip delay) are unspecified by the owner and remain unknown; the pilot cannot proceed without those values. Simulation results do not establish real-world performance or causality. Separate replications are not treated as independent samples for inferential purposes.
